One for copy, one for images, another for edits. But it ends up feeling like a duct-taped system that still needs constant attention. It’s not really solving the problem.Joel Erway193 views · 2d ago0:40If you manage client campaigns, you know how long it can take to get new ads live. Strategy, design, approvals, implementation. What should take days ends up taking weeks. And that delay becomes a real bottleneck.Joel Erway24 views · 3d ago0:24If you’re running ads for clients, you’ve probably felt how messy the process can get. Jumping between tools, copying things over, setting everything up manually. Just getting one ad live can take way more steps than it should. And over time, that inefficiency adds up.Joel Erway40 views · 6d ago0:24Agency owners, your clients already expect you to be using AI. They know what’s possible now. Faster results, better output lower costs. If it’s still taking weeks to get new ads out, that gap becomes hard to ignore. The real challenge is figuring out how to adapt your process to keep up.Joel Erway38 views · 6d ago0:08With AI ad tools everywhere, copy is no longer the hard part. The real problem is the workflow. Scaling ads means more creatives. More creatives mean more steps. More steps mean more time. More time means not scalable. I struggled with this firsthand. I hired expensive ad agencies. When it didn’t move the needle, I built a fully integrated system for Meta advertisers. One place to create copy and creatives. One place to review 30 ads on Monday. One click to push live ads. No jumping between tools. No broken workflow. Honestly?
